subject: Re: Demo request — Redwood demo & timezone coordination
messages:
From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 10:15:00 +0000
Subject: Product demo request — Acme x Redwood

Hi Marissa,

We'd love to schedule a demo of Redwood for our ML engineering team next week. We're primarily based in London (UTC+0) but have folks dialing in from Boston (ET) and Bangalore (IST). Can you propose a couple of slots that work for an hour-long intro + Q&A? Our calendar is fairly open on Tue/Wed mornings GMT.

Also — we use Calendly internally; if you send a scheduling link, please note that some of our teammates see times in EST even when their Macs are set to GMT, so if there's a way to force Europe/London timezone on the link that would help.

Thanks,
Emily Chen
Head of ML, Acme Corp
emily.chen@acme.com
+44 20 7000 0000

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 14:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Product demo request — Acme x Redwood

Hi Emily — great to hear from you, thanks for the context.

I just sent over my Calendly link to pick a 45–60 minute demo: https://calendly.com/marissa-demo. By default Calendly should detect your browser timezone but I know that sometimes browser/cached settings or Chili Piper profiles can cause the wrong display. If anyone on your side sees EST/PST instead of GMT, a couple of quick workarounds:

- Use the Calendly timezone parameter: https://calendly.com/marissa-demo?timezone=Europe%2FLondon (this forces the view to Europe/London)
- I can propose explicit slots in UTC and include an .ics invite with TZ info; that avoids the link UI entirely
- If Calendly still shows incorrectly, let me know the attendee emails and I can send a manual invite from our calendar (we include TZID in ICS files)

Proposed UTC slots (I converted from our default availability):
- Tue 3 Mar 2026 — 09:00–10:00 UTC
- Tue 3 Mar 2026 — 14:00–15:00 UTC
- Wed 4 Mar 2026 — 08:00–09:00 UTC (friendly for APAC attendees)

I've attached a short demo agenda that we typically use. If you prefer I can send a manual invite for any slot that works. Looping in Vivek (sales ops) in case we want to use a Chili Piper fallback for direct booking.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Attachments: MVP-demo-agenda.pdf (application/pdf, stub)

From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Product demo request — Acme x Redwood

Thanks, Marissa — I clicked the Calendly link and booked Tue 3 Mar at 10:00 because that looked like 10am GMT in the UI. After I accepted the event, my calendar created it at 10:00 but flagged it as PST for some reason, so one of my teammates in Boston is seeing 10:00 PST (which would be 18:00 GMT) — clearly wrong.

We suspect a DST/browser caching issue — two of our team members are on Macs that were recently updated and their system timezone prefs look fine, but Calendly still shows EDT/EST. Can you please either: (a) send an invite with explicit timezone info, or (b) manually create the event for Tue 3 Mar 09:00–10:00 UTC (that's 09:00 GMT) so all attendees get the same offset.

Apologies for the confusion — we have a couple of APAC folks who will join and want to make sure they don't get burned by the timezone mixup.

Best,
Emily

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 11:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Product demo request — Acme x Redwood

Hi Emily — thanks for the detail and sorry for the pain. Looping in Vivek (sales ops) and Lauren (SE) to coordinate a foolproof invite. Quick answers:

- I can create and send a manual .ics that sets TZID=Europe/London (or UTC) so calendar apps interpret it correctly.
- We'll also include the explicit UTC and local timezone string in the event title (e.g., "Redwood demo — Tue 3 Mar 09:00 UTC / 09:00 GMT / 04:00 EST") so any UI mismatch is obvious.
- For long-term: Vivek will check our Calendly account settings and Chili Piper profile options to ensure the timezone detection aligns with attendee IP/browser or the account profile. Some orgs set a default timezone in Calendly which overrides detection.

Lauren — for the demo itself, can you confirm you can do Tue 3 Mar 09:00–10:00 UTC? I'll send the .ics.

Thanks everyone,
Marissa

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Emily Chen <emily.chen@acme.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 20:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Product demo request — Acme x Redwood

Hi Emily / Marissa — Vivek here from Sales Ops. Short checklist and what I just did:

1) I created a manual calendar invite (attached) that uses UTC as the canonical timezone and includes TZID entries for Europe/London and America/New_York. That should render correctly in Outlook/Google/Mac Calendar. Attachment: acme_demo_invite.ics
2) I also re-generated a Calendly link with forced timezone parameter: https://calendly.com/marissa-demo?timezone=Europe%2FLondon — if someone opens that URL it will show slots in Europe/London. Note: some mobile apps or cached profiles still show the visitor's default, so the ICS is the safest option.
3) For future scheduling we can enable the Calendly account-level setting "Respect event timezone parameter" and/or add a short pre-booking note instructing attendees to verify the timezone in the top-right of the Calendly widget.

Marissa — I sent the .ics from my Google account and included the following in the event title: "Redwood demo (Acme) — Tue 3 Mar 09:00 UTC / 09:00 GMT / 04:00 ET"

Emily — please let me know if the invite looks correct when you accept.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com
Attachments: acme_demo_invite.ics (text/calendar, stub)

Quick follow-up: we have an APAC stakeholder who might need an earlier slot next week — can we keep the Calendly link live but prefer the manual ICS for multi-region scheduling? That combination would work for us (Calendly for quick internal bookings +/- ICS for cross-region invites).

Appreciate the help — looking forward to the demo.

Best,
Emily
